blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team's conftest.py sets AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and the other variables to testing before any client exists. Why, by the lesson?

options.text: So moto can find the developer's real account and copy its buckets into memory
options.says: Inside the mock the bucket exists only in moto's memory, and the account is moto's placeholder 123456789012.

options.text: So boto3 skips signing requests, which is what lets moto answer with no network
options.says: boto3 signs with whatever credentials it finds; with none, it refuses to sign (NoCredentialsError).

options.text: So the tests reach the team's AWS test account, whose key moto reads from them
options.says: No account is used: moto answers from memory, and testing belongs to no one.

options.text: So a request that escaped the mock signs with a key no one owns, and AWS refuses it
options.says: Right: a request that escaped the mock would be signed with the key testing, which belongs to no one.

origin.section: Fake Credentials Come First, So No Test Can Sign as Anyone

questions.stem: A function lists a bucket's results with a single list_objects_v2 call. Its moto test stores 1,500 result objects first. What does the call return under moto?

options.text: All 1,500 keys, because moto returns every key and only real S3 stops at 1,000
options.says: moto stops at 1,000 too: the output shows 'one list call: 1000 keys, IsTruncated True'.

options.text: 1,000 keys with no sign that more exist, so only a run against real S3 shows the bug
options.says: The response sets IsTruncated, as the output shows; the moto test catches it.

options.text: 1,000 keys with IsTruncated set, as S3 does, so this test catches the missing pages
options.says: Right: moto pages like S3; the paginator found all 1,005 where one call found 1,000.

options.text: An error that asks for a paginator, so the bug shows up as an exception in the test
options.says: No error: the single call returned 1,000 keys and IsTruncated True.

origin.section: moto Returns AWS's Errors and Pages, So Test Them

questions.stem: A moto test submits a Batch job named "run 0042!" with a 30-second timeout, then asserts the job ends SUCCEEDED. The test passes. What does that show?

options.text: Little: moto accepted a request AWS refuses, and it marks every job done without running it
options.says: Right: the output shows both accepted, and with use_docker off moto assumes every job succeeds.

options.text: That AWS will accept the request as well, because moto checks each request against AWS's rules
options.says: moto accepted a job name AWS forbids and a timeout under AWS's 60-second minimum.

options.text: That the solve ran and wrote its result, because moto runs each job's container to the end
options.says: With use_docker off, moto's documentation says job scripts are not executed and are assumed to succeed.

options.text: That the job role has the permissions it needs, because moto checks IAM on every call
options.says: moto's IAM page: by default it does not authenticate or authorize anything.

origin.section: moto Accepts What AWS Would Refuse, So Validate Before You Call
